_comment: Copy this file to config/profile.json and edit it. That copy is ignored by
git, so your home airports and budget stay on your machine.
This file is the whole point of Farewatch. The deal blogs broadcast; this
is what turns their firehose into a list that applies to you.
home_cities / home_airports: anywhere you would actually fly out of,
including airports you would drive to. Flights from anywhere else get
pushed down hard.
travel_style: budget | mid | luxury. Drives the food, lodging and local
transport estimates that turn a fare into a real trip cost.
wishlist: city or country names. Matched loosely.
preferred_months: deals whose headline names a month or season outside
these get demoted; deals that name no dates are treated as neutral.
max_trip_budget: all-in for the whole party, in home_currency.
require_reachable_origin: true hides every flight not leaving from your
airports. Leave false at first - you want to see what the feeds carry.
_home_airports_note: List the airports you would really use, nearest first, including any you
would drive to. A small home airport is the case this tool is built for:
the drive-to alternates matter far more from a regional field than from a
hub, because the fare difference is usually larger than the drive.
_unreachable_note: position - price the hop that reaches the deal's origin and rank the
honest all-in total. Start here: hiding unreachable origins
can empty the flight list entirely from a small airport.
hide     - drop them (the old require_reachable_origin behaviour)
show     - list them without pricing the hop

_comment: nonstop_from_base is every city your base airport reaches without a
connection, across every carrier serving it. Build it once from the
airport's own route map.
Recheck this list when routes change - it is the one part of the model
that goes stale on an airline's schedule rather than on its own.
